articles.headline: Brewers edge O's to tie team record for wins in a season with 97
articles.description: The Milwaukee Brewers tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore 1-0.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- The Milwaukee Brewers tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore 1-0 Saturday with the help of a fly ball lost in the sun by Orioles right fielder Rece Hinds.

Already assured of their fourth straight National League Central title and eighth playoff berth in nine seasons, the big league-best Brewers (97-58) matched the wins total of last year's team that finished 97-65.

Baltimore (75-80) fell four games behind the Chicago White Sox for the American League's last wild card with seven to play.

Robert Gasser (5-5) allowed three hits over seven innings, Abner Uribe worked around a leadoff single in the eighth, and Aaron Ashby pitched a perfect ninth for his third save, finishing the Brewers' 11th shutout this season and first 1-0 win.

Hinds lost Joey Ortiz's fly ball in the sun in the second inning and tumbled to the ground, and Gary Sánchez hit into a run-scoring groundout.

Trevor Rogers (10-11) struck out 10, walked one and allowed three hits in a season-high eight innings.

articles.headline: NFL Week 2 uniforms: Rams debut 'Classic Sol,' Ravens go all-white
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 2, led by a new alternate look from the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
Uniforms revealed in the offseason will make their respective debuts in Week 2. Fresh from their trip Down Under, the Los Angeles Rams look to win their first game of the season with a design rooted in its history.

Los Angeles will wear its "Classic Sol" alternate threads against the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football." The uniform honors the Rams' championship in 1951, with this season marking the 75th anniversary. A sol-colored jersey includes royal blue stitched and colored numbers. The three-stripe royal blue sleeve design is a direct nod to the uniforms worn in the 1951 season. The Giants will counter by going all-white.

The Baltimore Ravens underwent a closet redesign in the offseason, and with it came a new helmet and combination. Nicknamed "White Noise," Baltimore will pair all-white threads with the "Purple Rising" helmet against the New Orleans Saints. Baltimore originally revealed the purple lids in 2024, but tweaked them in April with a logo change, maintaining the metallic purple. It tops off a sleek new all-white look. 

It's an all-white look for the New York Jets as well, but from head-to-toe. New York unveiled new white helmets in July that differ from the throwback ones it typically wears with its classic uniforms. The Jets will pair it together with all-white jerseys and pants against the Green Bay Packers, who will wear their traditional home green on the road.

In the NFL "Rivalries" space, the Arizona Cardinals are the first to wear their design this season. Revealed last year, Arizona will rock it versus the Seattle Seahawks -- the same team they debuted it against in the previous campaign.

articles.headline: Sevilla's Luis García: 'It's a joke' Raphinha not Ballon d'Or nominee after another Barcelona hat trick
articles.description: Sevilla coach Luis García said it is a joke Raphinha is not among the Ballon d'Or nominees after watching the Barcelona forward score a hat-trick in his side's 3-1 defeat on Saturday.
articles.body:
Sevilla coach Luis García said it is a joke Raphinha is not among the Ballon d'Or nominees after watching the Barcelona forward score a hat trick in his side's 3-1 defeat on Saturday.

Raphinha followed up a midweek treble against Racing Santander with another at the Sánchez-Pizjuán as Barça made it seven wins from seven to start the LaLiga season.

The Brazilian forward has now scored 12 goals in the league -- and 14 in all competitions -- after being converted to a striker this summer.

However, he was absent from the 30-player shortlist for the Ballon d'Or, the most-coveted individual prize in the game, which was announced earlier this month.

"It's a joke that he's not even nominated for the Ballon d'Or," Luis García said in the post-game news conference.

"He is a match winner, that's why I don't believe in these prizes. He does everything."

Sevilla had started well against Barça, taking the lead through Youssouf Fofana as they threatened to become the first side to take points off the Spanish champions this season.

However, like many teams before them over the last month, they could not deal with Raphinha, who levelled before the break and added two more goals in the second half.

"Barcelona are playing at the top level, although what interests me is Sevilla," Luis García added.

"Barça had to be at their best to beat us today. I am proud of the lads."

Raphinha's remarkable form has come after Barça coach Hansi Flick repositioned him as a No.9 following the summer departure of Robert Lewandowski and the club's failure to land Julián Álvarez.

Saturday's hat trick came just hours after Barça sporting director Deco had confirmed an agreement is in place for Raphinha to sign a new contract until 2030, with his current deal up in 2028.

"For the club, it's the best decision to renew Raphinha's deal," Flick said.

"When you see how he connects with the fans, with the team ... He's a leader.

"This season he's been spectacular. The second half today was incredible. We know the quality of Raphinha and we're very happy about him, he gives us a lot.

"The decision to play him through the middle was made by the coaching staff, but with these numbers in these eight games, he's very happy to play as a No.9 as well."

- Deco confirms Barcelona contract extensions for Raphinha, Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart

- José Mourinho rejects Real Madrid, Barcelona comparisons: LaLiga 'a marathon'

- Lamine Yamal says he has experienced racism 'a thousand times'

The victory extended Barça's perfect start to the season to eight wins in all competitions heading into the international break.

Despite that, Flick still saw things against Sevilla he did not like.

"It was a difficult game, especially in the first half," he said.

"We also gave away the ball too easily a lot, that's not usually our level and our standard."

The win takes Barça six points clear at the top of the table temporarily, with second-placed Real Madrid in action on Sunday against rivals Atlétic

articles.headline: Beltran won't rule out return but no current interest in Mets job
articles.description: Carlos Beltran wouldn't rule out interviewing to become manager of the Mets, a job he left before he ran a single game in 2020, but he didn't sound all that interested.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- Carlos Beltran wouldn't rule out interviewing to become manager of the New York Mets, a job he left before he ran a single game in 2020, but he didn't sound all that interested.

His No. 15 was retired by the team Saturday before its next-to-last home game of a disappointing season in which Carlos Mendoza was fired June 26 as the high-spending team skidded to a losing record.

"Being a manager in Major League Baseball is a huge commitment -- very huge commitment," Beltran said before the ceremony, in which he was also inducted into the Mets Hall of Fame. "I'm not saying that I'm not willing to take that commitment, but right now, at the position where I am today in life, I love to be a dad, I love to be a husband, I love to be involved in the Carlos Beltran Academy in Puerto Rico.

"And being a manager, you would not be able to do that full time," Beltran added with a laugh.

A nine-time All-Star, Beltran was hired as the Mets' manager on Nov. 1, 2019, but left 76 days later in the fallout from the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal. Beltran was the only Astros player mentioned by name in Major League Baseball's report that concluded Houston broke rules by using electronics to steal signs en route to the 2017 World Series title.

 

Beltran is the 12th member of the Mets to have his number retired and the 38th person inducted into their Hall of Fame. He returned to the Mets in 2023 as a front office special assistant.

"Right now, I love what I'm doing," Beltran said. "I believe that the opportunity the Mets are giving me to be part of the organization and be able to comment on the things I experienced as a baseball player -- to hopefully continue to add value to the decisions that they're making and bring perspective on how I see things."

Mendoza was fired by president of baseball operations David Stearns on June 26 following a 34-47 start, and the Mets entered Saturday 36-37 under interim manager Andy Green, who wants to return to a front office role next year.

"Whatever step forward we do, I know it's going to be for the benefit of the organization," Beltran said. "And being honest, I think Andy has done a good job. He has done an incredible job for the Mets."

Elected to baseball's Hall of Fame in January, Beltran hit .280 with 149 homers, 559 RBIs and 100 stolen bases while winning three Gold Gloves in six-plus seasons for the Mets from 2005 to 2011.

"I think my skin got thicker playing in this city, which is good," Beltran said. "Because of the moments that I experienced here, I'm better. I'm better in every aspect. I want to use those experiences to continue to share it with the next generation -- share it with all the people that might be filling the same shoes that I filled."
